  • ✅ DER-11 Field type from a macro_rules $T:ty fragment: accepted like the type written directly, instead of rejected as an unsupported syn::Type::Group (test shrink_wrap/tests/macro_ty_fragment.rs).
  • ✅ DER-12 Display from doc comments: a display directive writes core::fmt::Display and core::error::Error (borrowed and owned) from the first doc line of each variant/struct, {field} filled in, #[display("..")] to override; a variant with neither is a compile error. Error enums need no hand-written Display on hosts (docs/serdes/derive_reference.md; test shrink_wrap/tests/display.rs).
  • ✅ DER-13 Sparse structs: #[derive_shrink_wrap(sparse, ..)] on a struct of Option<T> fields (borrowed and owned) encodes it as an OptionAnyVec (SW-55), one slot per field in declaration order or at #[slot = N] (increasing, gaps allowed, a present value in a gap is Error::OptionAnyVecUnknownSlot); a nested sparse struct is one slot. Fields are only appended. A non-Option field or a combination with final_structure / sized / self_describing / fixed_layout / head_tail is a compile error. For the per trait level <Level>Update of SRV-18 (docs/serdes/layouts.md, docs/evolution/rules.md; test shrink_wrap/tests/sparse.rs, fuzz shrink-wrap-option-any-vec). ww_self carries the flag (ItemStruct::sparse, Field::slot, TOOL-11), so a dynamic decoder (ValueOwned, the ww CLI, wire_weaver_py) reads a sparse struct correctly.
  • 📋 DER-5 #[since = "x.y.z"] on fields — generate correct evolution code from it (TODO in shrink_wrap_derive/src/lib.rs).
  • 📋 DER-6 Check that TailBytes ends the outer type too — a struct ending in TailBytes used as a non-last field of an outer sized / final_structure type ("last in the first Unsized type on the way up") is not visible to the derive; needs a marker on the type, e.g. an associated const, and a compile-time assertion in the outer type.
  • 📋 DER-7 Prefix enum discriminants · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 DER-16 Where clauses naming the borrowed lifetime, for owned types — a generic type bounded on its lifetime (enum Batched<'i, T> where Timed<T>: SeriesColumns<'i>) can't be derived with owned: the owned side has no 'i and would need the bound as for<'i> SeriesColumns<'i>. ww_client_server::observe::Batched / BatchedOwned (API-39) are written by hand for that.
  • ✅ DER-8 #[cfg(..)] on enum variants — a variant keeps its discriminant in every configuration, a build without it reads Error::EnumVariantDisabled (docs/serdes/derive_reference.md). First user: ww_numeric::NumericValue, one cargo feature per number type (32 to 8 bytes in RAM with 32-bit types only). Not yet: #[cfg] on fields (it would change the wire format, should be a compile error), ww_si enums.

items.title: API model and codegen (API)
items.text:
• ✅ API-1 Methods, properties, streams and sinks, nested traits (docs/api/overview.md).
  • ✅ API-2 Arrays of resources with ValidIndices and a built-in array size getter returning a range or list.
  • ✅ API-3 Global traits from ww_stdlib (impl Trait) and trait attachments (examples/all_gpio).
  • ✅ API-4 Results: methods return RpcResult (Ready, Defer, Unimplemented), properties return GetResult/SetResult, with user errors and property errors.
  • ✅ API-5 Request Context in every handler: seq, medium, event out, deferred replies.
  • ✅ API-6 Event, EventKind and error builders.
  • ✅ API-7 match on index slices, the base of multi-read support.
  • ✅ API-8 build.rs codegen via gen_server/gen_client, as an alternative to the proc macro.
  • ✅ API-9 Full name chains in generated names (fixed the event_sideband collision).
  • ✅ API-10 Type paths from Cargo: trait source path, external types in API crates as full paths.
  • ✅ API-11 Sync and async servers, async / blocking / promise clients from the same trait.
  • ✅ API-28 Credit-based flow control for sinks — #[credit] sink!(..): the device grants credit in bytes of items (the serialized value of each write, never split; the grant of an Ack since API-34), so a receive buffer holds as many items as fit whatever their sizes; the host waits when out of credit (async, blocking, try_send), writes carry the byte position of their first byte so a lossy medium resumes with go-back-N from have (Resend, Query), flush() waits for the final ack. No deadlock: generated <SINK>_MAX_ITEM_BYTES (from MAX_SIZE, MaxLen bounds included) and SinkCredit::sized_for() check at compile time that the buffer holds the largest item and cap the re-grant threshold, the host fails an item bigger than the buffer with StreamError::ItemTooBig. Device state in ww_stream::sink::SinkCredit (API-34), dynamic and Python clients too. Used by ww_dfu StageBulk::plan. For bulk transfers (chunky OTA plans over LTE-M/LoRa/UDP), UART bridges, CAN tx. See also CLT-18 backpressure (docs/api/credit_sinks.md, tests/credit_sink).
  • ✅ API-42 Credit-sink positions without a session limit · v0.5 — host (SinkTx) and device (SinkCredit) count positions in u64, the wire carries them modulo 2^28 (ww_stream::sink::POS_MODULUS, at most 4 bytes as a UVlq32), the receiver extends them from the position it expects (serial number arithmetic). The buffer is at most MAX_WINDOW (64 MiB, a quarter of the modulus), checked at compile time by sized_for, and the host never has more in flight; one fixed modulus on every link, nothing negotiated at the open. Tested over a seeded lossy link (loss, duplicates, reordering, reconnects) with sessions starting near the wrap and far past 4 GiB (docs/api/stream_protocol.md#positions-wrap-at-256-mib).
  • ✅ API-43 Generic types in APIs · v0.5 — generic structs and enums (DER-14, Timed<Ampere>, Window<4>, Reading<i16>, Tagged<'i, T>) as method arguments and return values, properties, stream items and fields. The API model (ww_self 0.3) has generics: each definition once with its type and const parameters (Type::Param, Length::Param), each use a Type::Instance with its arguments (types, integer/bool values, a const parameter passed on, defaults filled in by codegen); generic definitions are in crate snapshots, so ww_si::Timed is left out of introspection data like any known type. Generated code uses the types as written. Hosts check untrusted introspection data and instantiate it (ww_self::generics::prepare: indices, argument count and kinds, no cycles through generic definitions, nesting depth, number and size of instances bounded; dynamic decoding bounded by a value budget), so the dynamic client, ww and Python see concrete types; the evolution check compares parameters by position and kind (docs/types.md#generic-types-in-an-api, docs/evolution/rules.md#generic-types; tests tests/generics, ww_self unit tests, fuzz target introspection). Breaks the introspection format: hosts and devices must be built with the same ww_self. Generic traits (#[ww_trait] trait T<X>) are not supported.
  • ✅ API-44 Self-referential types in APIs · v0.5 — types that contain themselves through RefBox or a list (enum Expr<'i> { Neg(RefBox<'i, Expr<'i>>), Lit(i32) }, struct Tree<'i> { children: RefVec<'i, Tree<'i>> }), directly or through other types, as method arguments and return values, properties, stream items and fields. Codegen puts each definition into the API model once, referring to its own index; a cycle through a generic definition is an error. Hosts check untrusted introspection data (ww_self::generics::validate: cycles found with Tarjan's algorithm, only through Box/Vec, never through a generic definition, depth bounded by the sum of a cycle's definitions), and every walk over types stops at a definition it is already in (layout, compatibility check, names, definitions, default values: the first enum variant that doesn't contain the enum); values decode as deep as the reader allows (MAX_DECODE_DEPTH, ~90 levels on a 2 MiB stack in a debug build), Python objects are depth bounded (docs/types.md#self-referential-types-refbox; tests tests/recursive, ww_self/wire_weaver_core/ wire_weaver_client unit tests, fuzz target introspection). ww_si::SIExpr is one (STD-37).
  • ✅ API-45 Type aliases in APIs · v0.5 — pub type Volt = Quantity<VoltUnit>; and generic aliases (type Reading<T> = Timed<Quantity<T>>, const parameters too) in every API position, found like structs and enums (lib.rs, modules, use imports, globs, other crates); the right-hand side is converted in the alias' crate with each parameter replaced by its argument. The API model has no alias definitions (what an alias names is used directly, ww_si generic D2 a); alias definitions in ww_self are an idea for later. PhantomData fields (DER-15) are left out of a struct's definition, the parameter stays in its generics (ww_self::generics::prepare accepts that). Tests tests/generics (property, method argument, inside Timed, a PhantomData marker, dynamic client), wire_weaver_core unit tests, ww api tree (docs/types.md#type-aliases). use .. as .. renames are followed (API-46).
  • ✅ API-47 Resend and resume from inside a multi-unit event · v0.5 — an event of several units (a block, a batch, API-41) may be asked for again from a position inside it: a Resend there, or a resume from a cursor user code confirmed in the middle of it (AckMode::Explicit). The device sends the event that holds the position whole (StreamStore::read returns it for every store), the host's Receiver takes it with Verdict::Accept { skip } (also for ranges it had before a resume), PositionedStream gives the new units. Fixed with it: Resend no longer counts as an acknowledgement on the device (the store kept less than an explicit host had confirmed), acknowledgements and resends are valid up to the highest position sent (a late Resend on a reordering link stalled a backfill), the store is released when the backfill run ends in next_event. Tests ww_stream tests/sim.rs (batches of 1..64 units, a resend from every position inside, a resume cursor inside a batch, chaos with acks inside batches), wire_weaver_client stream_e2e_tests (docs/api/stream_protocol.md#positions-inside-an-event).
  • ✅ API-46 Codegen names types by their module path · v0.5 — each struct and enum records the path other crates name it by (ItemStruct::path / ItemEnum::path in ww_self, None at the crate root): the shortest one through pub mods and pub use re-exports (by name, renamed, glob); a type re-exported under another name is named that way, a type no other crate can reach is an error naming it. Its identity in its crate is path and name (units::Volt and a root Volt are two definitions): generated code names types by it (a type in a pub mod needs no root re-export, the ww_si 0.2 layout of a marker units::Volt next to the alias Volt works), snapshots take #[derive_shrink_wrap] types and unit marker structs from pub mods too, and SkippedFullVersion::type_name, signature resolution, inline_skipped and the definition cache look definitions up by it. Part of signatures, so introspection data and API hashes changed (snapshots saved again). The walker follows use .. as .. imports, and converts the arguments of a::b::Ty<Arg> where they are written. Tests tests/module_paths (pub module, lifetime two modules deep, rename, root re-export, re-export under another name, two equal Points, Quantity<units::Volt> next to a root Volt), tests/generics (ww_si layout as property, method argument, inside Timed), wire_weaver_core unit tests (a snapshot with units::Volt and a root Volt saved through RON and put back in an API) (docs/types.md#types-in-modules).
  • ✅ API-31 Stream functions — #[stream(T, counted)] fn name(args) -> Result<A, E> and #[counted] / #[reliable] stream!(name: T): every stream (plain ones too) is opened by calling it (RequestKind::StreamOpen), with typed arguments and result; the device's handler named like the stream decides, Ok starts a session, close_<name> closes it. Counted and reliable streams keep their state in what stream_<name>() returns (ww_stream::tx::Counted / Reliable), resume by cursor (name_resume(cursor)), answer a read with their StreamStatus (name_status()), send with stream_data_ser().<name>_send (counted) or push into the store with <name>_push (reliable), which the generated poll_streams sends by priority between requests and resends on the host's Resend; ww api scaffold, introspection (ApiItemKind::StreamFn), compatibility check and API diff know them. Includes API-15. Not yet: reliable streams in resource arrays (poll_streams refuses them), the open arguments in StreamStatus, stream functions in the dynamic client and Python (CLT-23), streams that detach by themselves when the link goes down (a resume re-attaches) (docs/api/stream_reliability.md, tests/streams_reliable).
  • ✅ API-16 Optional items — #[optional] / #[optional(group)] on a trait's methods, properties and streams; a server leaves them out with ww_codegen!(.., omit = ["i2c.pullups"]) or omit_if(<cfg>) = [..] (the user crate's features), pays no dispatch arm and writes no handler (about 100 bytes of flash per item on Cortex-M). Only optional items can be left out (compile error otherwise). A call answers Unimplemented from the level's fallback arm (id < ITEM_COUNT), the device's model lists the omitted items (ww_self omitted, root_omitted), so the generated and dynamic clients and Python fail locally with NotImplementedByDevice; ww api scaffold --omit, CLI tree and Python show them (docs/api/optional_items.md, tests/traits). Not yet: #[optional] on ww_impl!, the GUI (wire_weaver_tool).
  • ✅ API-32 Per-method error lists — #[errors(Common(InUse), Nack, ..)] on a trait method, a stream function (the open's Result error) or above a property! with an error type (its reads and writes): checked against the error enum when the trait is parsed (a compile error on a wrong name), in the API model (ww_self Method, StreamFn and Property errors), generated client and rustdoc # Errors with each variant's doc line, ww api tree, Python help(), ww api check (compatible); the generated and dynamic clients warn when a device returns a variant outside the list, tests fail (tests_common). Nothing on the device (docs/api/methods.md#error-lists, tests/methods, tests/properties, tests/streams_reliable). Not yet: the generated client's property reads (their errors are raw bytes, so only the dynamic client checks them); the GUI (wire_weaver_tool).
  • 📋 API-12 Calculate max path depth in server codegen · v0.5 — MAX_DEPTH is hardcoded to 16 in wire_weaver_core/src/codegen/api_server.rs.
  • 📋 API-13 Error system, remove unwraps from codegen · v0.5 — report errors with spans instead of panicking.
  • 📋 API-14 Load API crates from crates.io · v0.5 — the crate walker handles path and workspace dependencies; crate = "version" dependencies hit a todo!() in wire_weaver_core/src/transform/crate_walker.rs. Also dependencies from git (backlog). Every crate downloaded from crates.io has only such dependencies, so until this is done a published API crate whose API uses another crate's types or traits doesn't compile for its users or on docs.rs (DOC-6).
  • 💡 API-33 Narrow error types per method — generated per-method error enums with the crate enum's discriminants, as server handler return types only (narrow_errors = true), for a compile-time contract on the device. Explored and not recommended for clients: friction in every driver crate.
  • ✅ API-35 Stream functions with a borrowed error type · v0.5 — a stream function whose Result error has a lifetime (#[stream(I2cRecord<'i>, counted)] fn records(..) -> Result<(), I2cError<'i>>, every IO family error since it holds CommonError<'i>) compiles on the server with the handler signature ww api scaffold prints (RpcResult<Result<(), I2cError<'_>>>, an error borrowed from the server), for plain, counted and reliable streams, sync and async servers: the generated dispatch takes the Ok value out of the result before it opens the stream's state (tests/streams_borrowed_error). An Ok value that borrows from the server still can't.
  • ✅ API-36 Const items served from a value · v0.5 — a const NAME: T; of a #[ww_trait] is served without a get_<name> handler: the server struct implements the generated <RootTrait>Consts with const NAME: T = ..; (a Rust const) or, picked with const_model = "NAME=fn", fn name(&self) -> T for a value fixed at boot or link time (OTP, chip id, build id); names carry the trait item chain prefix (BOARD_BOARD / board_board). ww api scaffold --const-model prints the impl. Clients read a const once per connection, then answer from a cache (generated, dynamic and Python clients, promises too); ww introspect shows const values (tests/consts, docs/api/properties.md). ww_firmware_info, ww_board_info, ww_uid and ww_user_info servers use it.
  • ✅ API-38 Observe requests · v0.5.x — RequestKind::Observe on a trait level: per property Off, OnChange, Periodic or OnChangeOrBeat and a byte budget, the device answers with what it granted; updates arrive as one EventKind::PropertyUpdate per level carrying any subset of its properties (SW-55). Only +observe properties can be observed. Protocol ww_client_server::observe (docs/std_library/ww_client_server.md), device side SRV-18, host side CLT-28 (docs/api/observing.md, tests/observe).
  • 💡 API-37 Const values in the introspection blob — a codegen option putting the values of const items into the device's introspection data, so ww info gets them with the link setup and no extra reads. Costs flash per device, so not a default.
  • ✅ API-41 Batched streams and properties on Series — a stream or property opts into batching (+batched/batched, no size in the API: the device owns the batch size through its own config, default 32, the host picks latency) and sends Series<Timed<T>> (SW-60) batches instead of one item per event (device-side Batcher, reliable streams storing encoded batches so a resend costs no re-encoding); the same mechanism under API-39's batched property samples and a batched observe slot. Designed, with motor-demo numbers backing it (integer storage over floats, default batch 32, autoranging cost cheap); the batch store and size bounds are in (SW-62). In: the device side, ww_stream::batch (Batcher with two stores handed between a producer, also an interrupt, and the event loop through one atomic word, sealing on size, age and budget, encoding in the event loop; Outbox for observe; Batched reliable and counted streams), and batched streams end to end: batched / batched(untimed) in #[stream(..)] and #[batched] on stream! for plain, counted and reliable streams, StreamOpen { max_age_us }, generated <name>_push (O(1), interrupt-safe) and poll_streams encoding sealed batches, typed clients giving items one by one with their own time or whole batches (recv_batch), tests/streams_batched; the dynamic client giving the same (DynPositionedStream/DynStream, no generated code, ApiItemKind::StreamFn::batch_item_ty), ww stream <path> [--batches] and Python's recv_batch() (numpy columns, ww_self::SeriesColumn::from_items) (piece 6, no-arg streams only); batched observe is API-39. Docs: docs/api/batching.md (how-to, sealing, budgets, the motor demo's numbers). Motor demo (motor_sim repo): every Foc property and Control's 13 measured values are +observe+batched.
  • ✅ API-39 Batched property samples (observe every sample) — a ro+observe+batched property observed in ObserveMode::Samples { every_us, max_age_us } sends every sample the device takes as a Series<T> in its Batched<T> slot of the level's update, their times shared by the level (API-49) (docs/api/observing.md#every-sample-batched, tests/observe_batched). In: parsing and the model (ApiItemKind::Property::batched), the mode validated and clamped (ObserveLimits::samples_max_age_us), generated <Level>Sampler::sample(t, ..) (O(1), interrupt-safe after ObserveBatches::split()), double-buffered stores and a level outbox encoded in poll_properties with several updates per call, missed for lost samples and dropped batches, typed observers per sample, the dynamic client, ww observe --samples and Python (recv() samples, recv_batch() columns). Motor demo (motor_sim repo) on it, measured through the real generated code: docs/api/batching.md, and sample() itself in an interrupt on an STM32H725 next to observe cells (API-50, docs/api/batching.md#observe-cells-measured).
  • ✅ API-49 One time column per observe level (shared clock) — the samples a sample(t, ..) call takes for a level's +batched properties share one time column per update: EventKind::PropertyUpdate::sample_times (Series<Second>) next to t, the Batched::Samples slots untimed, Batching::SharedClock in introspection. A level keeps one batcher of rows (time and every value), its Samples entries share the finest every_us and the shortest max_age_us. Against a time column per property (21 FOC properties, n = 32, DeltaPacked): -36 % bytes, -52 % encode cycles on an STM32H725, -46 % instructions on Cortex-M3/M4F (docs/api/observing.md#which-rates-fit-an-mcu, tests/observe_batched).
  • ✅ API-50 Observe cells: sampling a level from an interrupt in place — ww_codegen!(.., observe_cells = "root_foc") puts a level with +batched properties on a ring of atomics instead of <Level>Sampler::sample: a const fn <Level>Cells<R> (a static, or an Arc), one <Level>Writer with a setter per property (relaxed stores where the value is computed) and commit(t) (the level's gate and grid, release fences, no lock), its reader in ObserveBatches::new / init; poll_properties copies the rows into one staging batch and sends them as the sampler's (same wire; a row the writer laps is missed, never sent mixed). Opt-in per level, the default stays. Built on shrink_wrap::series::SeriesCells (series(cells) derive, ww_si and numbers have it). On an STM32H725 a row of the motor demo's 21 FOC values takes 354 cycles at opt-level = "z" against 412 through sample() (328 against 419 at 3), 44-52 B of stack against 108-116 B, the same RAM. ww api scaffold --observe-cells. Writer and reader on two threads tested under miri (just miri). (docs/api/observing.md#cells-sampling-from-an-interrupt, tests/observe_batched, examples_mcu foc_observe.)
  • ✅ API-52 A cheaper observe poll — poll_properties of a level with +batched properties spends its cycles on the codec, not on bookkeeping, with the same bytes: a batch whose worst case doesn't fit the outbox's free room is written into it straight away and measured only when it didn't fit, a measure counts each column from the store (shrink_wrap::series::count_store_series) instead of rebuilding it into the scratch, the outbox keeps its batch count and offsets (LevelBatch::column_after), and a cells level copies only the time and the observed columns out of its ring (a column observed mid-batch is copied for the staged rows afterwards, seqlock-checked). On an STM32H725 the poll that encodes a 32-row batch of the 21 FOC properties takes 100 k cycles instead of 191 k at opt-level = 3 and 169 k instead of 513 k at "z" (cells 107 k / 180 k), so all 21 at 25 kHz are 17 % of the core with the rows instead of 30 % (27 % instead of 77 % at "z"); a cells drain of 3 of 21 observed columns 4.4 k instead of 9.2 k. The high rates moved little (3 values at 400 kHz 74 % of the H725 instead of 78 %, 1 MHz 181 %, 2 values at 2 MHz 313 %): their polls are the codec and each column's framing now (docs/articles/series.md#high-rates-a-few-values-at-400-khz-to-2-mhz, examples_mcu foc_observe, high_rate, ww_stream cells_tests).
  • 📋 API-17 Methods arguments to a user struct · v0.5.x.
  • 🚧 API-18 Size analysis · v0.5.x — maximum buffer usage in the worst case, auto-calculated buffer sizes for events, arguments and outputs. Done: MAX_SIZE of types (SW-19) and per-method <METHOD>_REQUEST_MAX_LEN / <METHOD>_RESPONSE_MAX_LEN consts in no_alloc servers, checked at compile time against a buffer in tests/bounded and examples_mcu/mcu_qemu. Missing: consts for properties, streams and sinks, the largest of all of them for a whole API (to size ww_device buffers such as UdpBuffers<MAX_MESSAGE_LEN> automatically), paths of nested traits counted exactly (now the worst case of the full path), the same consts on the client.
  • 📋 API-19 Change dispatcher match order to process common requests faster · v0.5.x.
  • 🚧 API-20 Trait paths on the server side · v0.5 — servers serve PathKind::GlobalFull requests (crate, version and trait name) wherever the trait sits in the tree, ErrorKind::TraitNotFound otherwise (tests/cross_version, docs/api/addressing.md). Missing: PathKind::GlobalCompact (compact ids of traits are not in the API model yet, none is assigned), traits under a resource array.
  • 📋 API-21 no_alloc = false servers — don't compile today.
  • ⛔ API-22 Implement the same trait several times → enum selector · v0.5.x — stalled. At least print a proper error when a trait is implemented twice (tests/traits_api).
  • ⛔ API-23 Index chain array → named arguments · v0.5.x — stalled. Generating ad-hoc structs with named index fields might be a good ergonomic: users see the names through IDE lookup instead of guessing array indices.
  • 📋 API-29 Bounds of resource array indices · v0.5.x — stream!(adc[8]: u16) or motor[1..=4], checked by the server before a handler is called and visible in introspection (docs/api/arrays.md). Lengths of lists and strings inside a resource's type are bounded with MaxLen (SW-19). With a bound, observed properties (SRV-18) can get a table per array element: until then a trait level in a resource array can't be observed (STD-31 ww_gpio pin level waits for it).
  • 🚧 API-30 Counted and reliable streams · v0.5 — counted streams put a head in every event (flags and a length-coded 64-bit pos in units the device names when it sends, the event's units, lost, optional device time t), so drops on the device, link losses and duplicates are reported exactly and item types carry no seq / lost / t fields (IO family D4, D5). Reliable streams add Ack / Resend / Query (go-back-N, grants in bytes), keep unacknowledged events in a store, resume by cursor after a reconnect with the latest values first and the backlog beside them; a send scheduler with priorities between streams; typed cnt counters (docs/api/stream_reliability.md). Done, the protocol core: wire types in ww_client_server::stream (StreamHead with its hand-laid encoding, byte-verified; StreamCursor, StreamOpened, EventKind::StreamItem, RequestKind::StreamOpen, the sideband), the ww_stream crate (Counted, Reliable, Receiver, RamRing, Scheduler, StreamCnt; sans-IO, no_std, tested over a seeded lossy link with random disconnects), ww_self::ApiItemKind::StreamFn, codegen (API-31), the host runtime (CLT-23). Missing: credit sinks on it (API-34). The persistent store is done (SRV-15).
  • 🧪 API-34 Credit sinks on the stream protocol · v0.5 — Ack / Query / Resend shared with reliable streams, sessions and resume for credit sinks, so a sink (UART tx, a DFU plan) continues after a reconnect. Positions count units the host names per item (1 by default, the payload's bytes for a byte sink), grants count bytes; positions stay as API-42 has them (u64 in state, modulo 2^28 on the wire), the host keeps at most MAX_WINDOW bytes and units in flight; streams keep their full UVlq64 positions (their gaps are unbounded). The host names the session in StreamOpen's cursor, so a repeated or late duplicate open (UDP) no longer resets a running session. Done: the protocol core, ww_stream::sink (SinkCredit on the device, SinkTx on the host), RequestKind::SinkWrite / SinkWriteUnits, and the switch-over: generated server code (open by StreamOpen, a read returns StreamStatus), the host Sink (send_units, open_session, a device that lost the session is reported), dynamic client and Python, ww_dfu, every test crate; the old Credit / CreditQuery / Resend, CreditWrite and ww_client_server::credit are gone, ResendFrom is Resend. Resume in the host API: Sink::cursor(), sinks in disconnect().keep_streams() / Commander::resume_streams() (the session goes on from where the device is, nothing repeated or lost), the generated <sink>_resume(cursor) after a host restart, StreamError::SinkSessionLost for a device that lost the session; Python Sink.cursor / resume / ww.SessionLost. Tests: wire_weaver_client event_loop/sink_e2e_tests.rs (reconnect in the middle of a transfer with lost writes, a rebooted device, a restarted host, a late duplicate open), tests/credit_sink, the 2C-APP-BULK DFU scenario. See docs/api/credit_sinks.md#resume. To check on hardware: TEST-26.
  • 💡 API-53 Sink functions — #[sink(T, credit)] fn uart_tx(config: TxConfig) -> Result<A, E>, the counterpart of stream functions (API-31): a sink opened with a configuration and a typed result, a new session exactly when the configuration changes. The wire has it (StreamOpen { args }); codegen and the host API are missing.
  • 💡 API-24 Guarded calls for critical resources · v0.5.x — for safety-critical actions, such as starting a motor or switching high power, a request that happens to match predefined bytes must not be enough. Add an extra check, e.g. a CRC over the resource identity and arguments (a "strict mode" per resource), or a request/response challenge before the call is executed.
  • 🚧 API-26 Generate C · v0.5.x, and an FFI example. Generated C comes from the ww_self model, not from the derive's AST: a generator run after the build, from an introspection bundle (e.g. ww gen c), writes .h / .c for an API's types on top of the C runtime (SW-43 c-runtime), later a device-side dispatcher, introspection as a const blob and ww_framer. None of that is there yet. The C header text fixed_layout (SW-44, SW-45) and head_tail (SW-46) print from the derive today moves to that generator over time. Other languages are generated the same way, from the model. The conformance matrix (TEST-23) is what keeps the generated code byte-equal to the derive.
  • 💡 API-27 Standalone definition files with custom syntax — APIs and types in their own files, with a friendlier syntax: nested levels, no macro calls, SI units. Tried twice already, approach with care:
  • at the very beginning of this repo, a YAML based language;
  • later, a big effort to support a custom syntax, which turned into a project of its own and took a lot of resources away from the actual work.

Plain Rust with #[ww_trait] and #[derive_shrink_wrap] is the current answer; revisit only with a concrete benefit that outweighs the cost of a parser, tooling and IDE support. - 💡 API-40 value_on_changed strings without an allocator — a no_alloc server's field for a MaxLen<&'i str, N> property is &'static str today, which a write can't fill; generate an shrink_wrap::ArrayString<N> field (SW-57) instead, and ArrayVec<T, N> for lists, so settings like a device label can be value_on_changed too (STD-32). - 💡 API-51 Stream codecs across items — any stream or observed property could send each item as a diff against the one before, generic over T, from the derive per leaf: integers as delta or delta of delta, floats XOR coded, enums, units, strings and bool as one "same" bit or the new value, a whole item "unchanged" bit; byte items (UART or CAN frames) XOR'd with the previous one or through a small no_std LZ window. Declared in the API (#[stream(T, codec = auto)]), in the introspection data so dynamic clients and Python decode it; keyframes on open, after a gap and every N items. It is how a string or a frame, which a Series batch can't take (no size bound), would get cheaper per item. Prior art: Gorilla, Sprintz, Chimp, ALP.

items.title: Server / device side (SRV)
items.text:
• ✅ SRV-1 no_std, no-alloc server, IO-free generated code.
  • ✅ SRV-2 Sans-IO DeviceLink, async Server with wait()/handle() for a user-owned event loop, and blocking::Server.
  • ✅ SRV-3 Fully split TX and RX flows for every transport (fixed the half-duplex interlock), framing without IO.
  • ✅ SRV-4 User handlers called straight from the RX loop, transport glue extracted into ww_device.
  • ✅ SRV-5 Device descriptors: serial, WireWeaver version, API id, version, hash and user label in the USB interface string.
  • ✅ SRV-6 Media: USB (embassy), RTT, WebSocket and UDP (both also on embassy-net).
  • ✅ SRV-7 UDP device medium — ww_device::udp, one frame per datagram over any datagram socket, one host at a time, another host takes over by starting link setup (docs/transport/udp.md).
  • ✅ SRV-15 Stream stores and backfill — ww_stream::store: what a reliable stream (API-30) keeps until the host acknowledges it: RamRing (API-30) and LogStore, a power-cut safe log on a block device (feature log-store; SdMedium on an embedded-sdmmc BlockDevice with sdmmc, NorMedium on an embedded-storage-async NorFlash with nor-flash) that keeps session, positions and clock epochs across reboots; drop-newest or drop-oldest when full, counted exactly. Tested with a power cut at every write (ww_stream/src/tests/log_store.rs); docs/api/stream_stores.md.
  • ✅ SRV-16 Persistent RAM store — ww_stream::store::PersistentRamRing (feature persistent-ram): a reliable stream's store in .uninit RAM that survives a soft reset (fault → reset), for the logs before a crash (STD-26). Header slots and records checked by CRC at boot, so garbage after a power-on is never taken for data; continues session and positions like LogStore, a new clock epoch per boot. Tested with a fault after every byte written (ww_stream/src/tests/persistent_ram.rs); docs/api/stream_stores.md.
  • ✅ SRV-18 Observed properties on the device — servers of APIs with +observe properties answer Observe requests (API-38) and send PropertyUpdates from the generated poll_properties: ObserveState with one table per trait level sized at compile time, a sparse <Trait>Update per level (DER-13), mark_changed_<name>() (called for value_on_changed writes), periodic properties sampled through their getter. A token bucket per level at the granted budget, earliest deadline first, at most one update per level per call, the rest slips and counts as missed; properties have a reserved share of the link (ObserveLimits::total_budget) next to stored streams. Observe is untrusted input: validated in full before anything changes, clamped, bounded work, refused per entry. Levels under a resource array answer OperationNotSupported until their bound is known (API-29), +observe properties in an array or #[optional] aren't observable yet. ww_stream::observe, docs/api/observing.md#the-device-side; tests tests/observe (fake clock, real host event loop), ww_stream/src/observe/tests.rs.
  • ✅ SRV-20 deferred-nested-levels Deferred return helpers on nested levels — <prefix>_<method>_send_return, _send_return_blocking and _ser_return_event are generated for deferred methods on nested trait levels too, named like the handler (plug_vbus_cycle_send_return); method_model patterns match the prefixed name. Test tests/methods (deferred_on_nested_level), docs/api/methods.md#deferred.
  • ✅ SRV-21 handler-model Sync handlers in an async server — ww_codegen!(.., handler_model = "device.settings.*|meter.reading=async, _=sync"): per item (regex over its dotted path, first match, _ the default, use_async without one) its handlers are async fn or plain fn; the dispatcher and poll_properties call sync ones without .await, a level whose items are all sync gets a plain fn dispatcher. A handler of the other kind is a compile error (wire_weaver::handler checks), so is a pattern that matches nothing. ww api scaffold --handler-model. Donguru: -20.2 KiB flash at z, -12.6 KiB at 3. docs/api/handlers.md; test tests/observe (a mixed server).
  • ✅ SRV-23 observe-table-unsized One observe table code for every level — ww_stream::observe::ObserveTable<S: ?Sized = [Slot]>: a level stores ObserveTable<[Slot; N]>, the methods (apply, plan, commit, ...) are compiled once, on ObserveTable<[Slot]>; LevelDesc is slices, the plan and the selection keep their per-slot state in caller storage (Due, Mark), and levels without observable properties answer Observe through one shared path (refuse_all). Donguru: −13.3 KiB flash at opt-level = 3, −9.4 KiB at z. ww_stream/src/observe.rs, docs/api/observing.md#the-device-side.
  • ✅ SRV-25 event-driven-observe No fixed observe tick — a device sleeps until something observed is due instead of polling every millisecond. ObserveState::next_wake(now_us) (ObserveTable::next_wake per level: the periodic grid, last + min of a changed property, last + max of a beat, a held level's bucket refill, a batch sealed or as old as allowed; None when nothing comes due without a change); a generated ObserveSignal any task or interrupt marks a property changed through (mark_changed_<name>()) or wakes the server task with, no lost wake between a change and the sleep (ww_stream::wake); with_wake on samplers and cells writers; ww_device::Server::wait_until(at); ww api scaffold prints the signal. Tests: ww_stream (polling only at next_wake sends what polling every µs does), tests/observe (fake clock: polls only on the grid, a change from another thread sent at once), tests/observe_batched. docs/api/observing.md#the-server-loop.
  • ✅ SRV-24 shared-observe-loop One observe loop for every level — the algorithm of poll_properties (plan, overhead, selection, measuring, writing, commit, missed counts, batches of samples) is ww_stream::observe's, sync: plan_level, select, write, ser_update. The generated poll_properties is one loop over the levels with one send site; per property it gives only a size and a write arm (through &mut dyn FnMut) and awaits its async getters (SRV-21) itself, reading an unbounded async value once. ObserveState::level / oldest_batch / remove_oldest_batch reach a level by its number. Donguru, on top of SRV-21 and SRV-23: −5.8 KiB flash at opt-level = 3, −5.0 KiB at z. ww_stream/src/observe.rs, docs/api/observing.md#the-device-side; tests tests/observe, tests/observe_batched, ww_stream/src/observe/tests.rs. A value that can't be had at write time is dropped alone (counted missed), the rest of the update goes; tested on Donguru B153A (plug with cc unimplemented).
  • ✅ SRV-22 error-seq-per-item Error sites numbered the same in every server — err_seq of an Error is no longer one counter across the generated server (705 numbers on Donguru) but fixed per site (ww_client_server::err_seq): item steps in step order and the same for every item (0 kind not taken, 1 decode, 2 handler, 3 encode, ..), level sites (40..), request sites (48..), deferred return (32..). With the build, the request path and the error kind it still pinpoints one site, and identical error arms are shared code: Donguru -1.5 KiB flash at z, -1.7 KiB at 3. Error::site(), the host prints Unimplemented at item site 2 (handler). docs/api/errors.md#where-on-the-device-an-error-came-from; tests tests/methods, tests/traits.
  • ✅ SRV-26 Device-side engine for I2C and SPI slaves — ww_bus_slave, no_std, sans-IO, no alloc: I2cSlave and SpiSlave do what STD-35's API promises, so a firmware only wires its peripheral's interrupts to them. I2C: the register map (pointer bytes, auto-increment, wrap at len, page wrap, read_only), host updates staged until the stop, the answer queue with Fill, Stretch { max } (deadline, resume, ReadWaiting) and Nack (acks_address), unsent for a TX FIFO loaded ahead. SPI: queue answers (idle, repeat_last, underrun) and SpiRegisters frames (address, rw bit, dummy bytes before read data), the answer picked at the first miso() (FIFO preload, rewind); 8-bit words only. Events built as I2cSlaveEvent / SpiSlaveFrame. const fn new for a static; 58-100 instructions per byte on a Cortex-M3 (examples_mcu/mcu_qemu bin qemu-bus-slave). docs/api/bus_slave.md, tests ww_bus_slave/tests. First firmware user: usb_io_fw IF-5 (rePort, RP2350B).
  • 🧪 SRV-19 ECC-safe STM32 flash for stores — mcu/ww_ecc_flash: EccSafeFlash wraps any NorFlash (embassy-stm32's Flash) and reads it one ECC word at a time; a word with an uncorrectable ECC error (power cut while programming or erasing) reads as zeros instead of an NMI (STM32G0, FLASH_ECCR.ECCD, through on_nmi() or feature nmi-handler) or a bus error (STM32H7, DBECCERR, ignored under FAULTMASK + BFHFNMIGN), so sequential-storage skips it. Never MultiwriteNorFlash. Blocking and async. docs/api/ecc_flash.md. On hardware: a G0B1 (B153A) store survives 3000 resets in the middle of its programs and erases (TEST-21), but a reset never tears a G0 flash word, so the zeros path itself still waits for a real power cut (TEST-21); H7 is built, not run on hardware.
  • ⛔ SRV-8 One crate per role for firmware and host · v0.5 — blocked on generated code using absolute paths. Agreed direction, instead of putting everything into wire_weaver behind features or splitting by std/no_std:
  • wire_weaver stays lean (shrink_wrap, macros, ww_version, result types) since every API crate and ww_stdlib crate depends on it;
  • ww_device re-exports wire_weaver, ww_framer, ww_link and gets features usb-embassy, rtt, udp, ws, defmt, embassy-time, std;
  • wire_weaver_client re-exports wire_weaver with transport features.

Requires: codegen emitting paths through the role crate (or a crate = ".." argument / proc-macro-crate; WIRE_WEAVER_REEXPORTS in the crate walker is partly there), and wire_weaver_usb_embassy building in the root workspace or merging into ww_device. Separately consider making wire_weaver's std default off.

  • 📋 SRV-9 Handle USB suspend/resume · v0.5 — run until suspend, wait for resume, loop (mcu/wire_weaver_usb_embassy). Later (v0.5.x): detect the host going to sleep and keep the connection, informing the device.
  • 📋 SRV-10 Collect error codes into an ELF section for easier error decoding · v0.5.x.
  • 📋 SRV-11 Link statistics in ww_device (TODO in link.rs).
  • 💡 SRV-12 std server on Tower · v0.5.
  • 💡 SRV-13 IPC over USB / multi-app devices / USB multiplexer · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 SRV-14 FPGA server · v0.5.x.

items.title: Client / host side (CLT)
items.text:
• ✅ CLT-1 std client with async, blocking and promise flavors, prepared call objects, no root() needed.
  • ✅ CLT-2 Generic sans-IO event loop over a Transport, independent TX and RX flows.
  • ✅ CLT-3 USB transport on nusb: endpoint addresses from descriptors, bulk with lower priority, vec recycling.
  • ✅ CLT-4 RTT transport over a debug probe, control block address from an ELF file.
  • ✅ CLT-5 WebSocket, UDP and in-process transports.
  • ✅ CLT-6 DynClient and dynamic resources, for APIs known only at runtime.
  • ✅ CLT-7 Introspection cache keyed by API hash with and without docs, with a download timeout.
  • ✅ CLT-8 Compatibility check on connect: each resource is checked against device introspection when the API hash differs.
  • ✅ CLT-9 Connection selectors, clear errors when no device is found, disconnect() releases the transport.
  • ✅ CLT-24 One ? per call — a method returning Result<T, E> gives Result<T, CallError<E>> (Device(E), Unimplemented { resource } or Client(Error)) from call, blocking_call and promises, a property with a user error type the same from write and write_promise, instead of Result<Result<T, E>, Error> and ??; Error::is_unimplemented() for items without an error type (docs/api/methods.md#client-side, tests/methods).
  • ✅ CLT-25 ww info and ww report · v0.5 — ww info shows firmware, board, ids, label and last reset of any device by global trait path, whatever its API version; ww report adds the counters, the stored defmt log and the crash's addresses named with the ELF, found by build id, as one file a tester sends; ww elf add <elf|archive> fills the ELF directory from an ELF or a release's <firmware>-<version>-elf.tar.zst (shared with cnt elf add, cnt_core::elf). Library crate ww_report (Contract, collect_info, collect_report), docs/std_library/device_contract.md, tests/device_report. The stored log is a stream and streams open on the absolute path only (CLT-23), so ww report reads the device's introspection data for the log's path; ww info needs none. Not yet: fetching the release archive by itself.
  • 🐛 CLT-30 Link setup gives up too early on slow RTT probes — the client sends GetDeviceInfo 5 times 50 ms apart (LINK_SETUP_RETRIES / LINK_SETUP_RETRY_INTERVAL in event_loop/core/tx.rs), 250 ms for every transport. Through a J-Link on omarchy-m1 (aarch64, probe-rs, each RTT write ~17 ms) most connects fail with "LinkSetup was not received from device after several retries" while the device is fine; with 40 retries they mostly work. Needs a per-transport budget (RTT: seconds) or one taken from the connect timeout. Found 16 Oct 2026.
  • ✅ CLT-28 Observing properties on the host · v0.5.x — generated std clients have observe(cfg) per trait level with +observe properties (an Observer of the level's <Trait>Update) and observe_<name>(mode) per property, fanned out from the level: one device subscription per level covering all its observers (merged modes, biggest budget), sent again when an observer comes, changes (configure) or goes, Off after the last one; <Trait>Observe typed settings and what was granted, <Trait>Latest latest-value cache with receive times; subscriptions sent again by resume_streams() after a reconnect; Error::Unsupported for a device whose API model predates API-38 (wire_weaver_client::observe, docs/api/observing.md#the-host-side, tests/observe, observe_e2e_tests). Not yet: levels under a resource array.
  • ✅ CLT-29 Series<T> in introspection and dynamic clients · v0.5.x — ww_self::Type::Series (and Field::series_opaque for #[series(opaque)] fields) in the API model, emitted by codegen; a dynamic decoder in ww_self reads a Series column by column from the type tree alone (ValueOwned::des_shrink_wrap_dyn gives the items, des_series_columns_dyn the columns), with the typed decoder's rules (restarts after enum and Option tags, evolvable structs both ways, declared defaults) and the decode budget bounding work and memory (a constant column costs no bytes); ww shows the items, Python decodes the items or numpy columns (decode_columns, masked where an item is in another variant or None). Dyn equals typed on the design's examples, on generated and on fuzzed series (fuzz target series-dynamic, tests/series, wire_weaver_py/tests/test_offline.py, docs/serdes/series.md#introspection-and-dynamic-clients). Writing too: ValueOwned::ser_shrink_wrap_dyn (and ser_series_dyn with a CodecPolicy) writes a Series from its items, the typed writer's bytes for the same policy (codec choice, restarts, struct heads, generics), so a dynamic client and Python write Series arguments and properties.
  • ✅ CLT-31 Quantities in dynamic clients, ww and Python · v0.5.x — a ww_si::Quantity<U> (ww_si 0.2 and later) is recognized from introspection data alone: a concrete definition records the generic one and arguments it was made from (ww_self::ItemStruct::instance_of, host-derived, rejected from devices, left out of signatures), the unit comes from ww_si::units::by_name, the Per / Times tree, or a marker of the API's own crate by name and docs. wire_weaver_client::quantity (DynQuantity: 3300 mV, {:#} 3.3 V, to_si_f64, to_value; DynUnit), ww introspect const values and ww observe print with symbols, Python ww.Quantity (value, prefix, exponent, storage, symbol, unit, dim, docs, to_si(); writes take a Quantity or a number in the unit) (docs/std_library/ww_si.md#in-ww-python-and-dynamic-clients, tests/quantities, wire_weaver_py/tests). Types are still named by their definitions (Timed<Quantity<Ampere>>), alias names need ww_self type aliases.
  • ✅ CLT-30 Link setup budget per transport · v0.5.x — the client re-sent GetDeviceInfo 5 times 50 ms apart (250 ms for every transport), so connecting through a debug probe (~17 ms per RTT write through a J-Link) mostly failed with LinkSetup was not received. Now a timeout per transport (USB, UDP, WebSocket 1 s, in-process 250 ms, RTT 10 s, one place: event_loop::transport::link_setup_timeout), retries back off (first after 1/20 of it, doubling up to ¼), ClientConfig::link_setup_timeout() and ww --link-setup-timeout-ms / WW_LINK_SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS / link_setup_timeout_ms in ww.toml override it (wire_weaver_client/src/event_loop/transport.rs, event_loop/core.rs tests). On a J-Link + STM32G0 over RTT the old 250 ms was not what failed in the test: connects succeeded with both budgets once TR-13 was fixed.
  • 🚧 CLT-10 Trait calls that work on any device · v0.5 — serial, user label, a CLI that works with all devices. ww list with filters and USB interface string metadata are done, and global trait calls on any device whatever its API version: ClientConfig::traits_only(), DynClient::global_attachment() (served through API-20, tests/cross_version), ww dfu reboot, ww counters (STD-25) and ww info / ww report (CLT-25). Missing: CLI commands for the other ww_stdlib traits (GPIO, UART, ...).
  • 📋 CLT-11 Typed property handles · v0.5 — RwProperty/RoProperty/WoProperty so that .prop_name().read(), .prepare_write(1).blocking(), .asynch().await work.
  • 📋 CLT-12 Stream receive timeout · v0.5 — and a beat timeout between updates.
  • 🔍 CLT-13 Typed attachments with TraitMarker · v0.5 — trait attachments exist (Attachment, examples/all_gpio); check whether a typed marker is still wanted.
  • 💡 CLT-14 no_std client (client = "raw") — documented as not working in ClientModel::Raw, its test is commented out in tests/traits. Its generated code serializes arguments into a fixed 128 byte scratch and then calls .to_vec(), which isn't no_std; it should write into a caller-provided buffer instead. The std clients (std_client, trait_client) already serialize with to_ww_bytes_owned() and have no size limit.
  • ✅ CLT-15 Multi read/write/call · v0.5.x — servers with multi_req = true dispatch MultiRead, MultiCall and MultiWrite (Same or Different args), each index answered on its own (Either<Error, value>), and answer malformed multi requests with errors instead of panicking (tests/multi_req). Client side: generic MultiRead/ MultiCall/MultiWrite tuple traits (any arity 2..=8, any depth, not just root 2-tuples), read_array/ call_array/write_array for homogeneous requests across an array's indices (List/Range/Mask32, Same or Different args chosen automatically), and a DynResource equivalent for the dynamic client (docs/api/multi_requests.md, tests/properties, tests/methods, tests/dynamic). Deferred methods inside a multi request are refused with OperationNotSupported.
  • 📋 CLT-32 Generic definitions from another revision by the evolution rules · v0.5.x — a definition a device leaves out that differs from the host's snapshot (an unpublished crate changed without a bump) is found in the definition cache and compared by the evolution rules, but only when it is not generic: for an instance of a generic definition (ww_si::Quantity<U>, Timed<T>) check_instances compares identity and signature only, so a docs-only change reads as incompatible. Compare the two generic definitions field by field with the arguments substituted. Found by STD-38 (wire_weaver_client compat::tests::other_revision now use the marker units::Volt).
  • 📋 CLT-16 Verify the hash of a cached API bundle · v0.5.x (wire_weaver_client/src/local_registry.rs).
  • 📋 CLT-17 Reliable requests over unreliable media · v0.5.x — a second, non-increasing seq number to guard against a lost reply for a request that was executed, when executing twice is not OK. Relevant for UDP.
  • 🔍 CLT-18 Backpressure — commands already go through a bounded channel (ClientConfig::cmd_queue_size), so user code should block or yield when the queue is full; add tests for it. A request sent while every request id is in flight waits for one. Flow control towards the device for sinks: API-28 credit-sinks.
  • 📋 CLT-19 Connection priority in the client config (TODO in config.rs).
  • 📋 CLT-20 Bound check of generated byte sink writes · v0.5.x — a sink!(x: MaxLen<RefVec<'i, u8>, N>) write from a generated client is sent as raw bytes without a length check, the device rejects a longer one (ArgsDesFailed); the dynamic client and Python already check before sending.
  • 🚧 CLT-21 Follow a device across a reboot into other firmware — for DFU (ww_dfu BootControl::reboot(Updater)): reconnect to the same device by serial number, whatever answers there, with a timeout. Done for USB: wire_weaver_client::follow (Follow, Bus, Found), and the RP2350 / RP2040 boot ROM as the updater: ww_picoboot (PICOBOOT host on nusb, SimRp2350 for tests), follow::rp2_update(), ww bootsel, tested end to end on a simulated device (tests/follow_reboot, docs/transport/follow_reboot.md). The PICOBOOT host moved to its own repo, picoboot_host (evaluated the crates.io picoboot 0.3.0 crate first: no sans-IO boundary to put SimRp2350 behind, no Image/UF2 handling, no orchestrated flash+verify, no chip_id/GET_INFO — adopting it would have meant donating most of ww_picoboot upstream anyway); WireWeaver depends on it as ww_picoboot (a path dependency on ../picoboot_host while its ELF support, IMG-4, is unlanded; a git dependency on github.com/vhrdtech/picoboot_host once it lands, until it is on crates.io). wire_weaver_client's picoboot feature (off by default) gates follow::rp2_update() and the ww_picoboot re-export, so a host app that only talks WireWeaver over USB doesn't pull in PICOBOOT; ww bootsel turns it on, and follow::rp2_update_with() (what tests/follow_reboot runs against a simulated device) needs neither it nor usb. ww bootsel flash takes a UF2, an ELF (detected by magic bytes, taken by its PT_LOAD segments' flash physical address — no objcopy/ elf2uf2 needed) or a raw binary. Missing: a run against a Pico 2 / rePort; RTT (another control block: a second ELF or a RAM scan) and UDP / WebSocket (the port may change); asking for the reboot from the CLI needs CLT-10.
  • 📋 CLT-22 One Sink::send for borrowed and owned items — owned types (FooOwned) implement only SerializeShrinkWrapOwned, so they go through send_owned; one send for both (a sink item trait, or the derive implementing both), then drop send_owned.
  • 🚧 CLT-23 Stream positions, gaps and resume on the host · v0.5 — Commander::prepare_stream_open / prepare_stream_resume (what generated code calls, PreparedStreamOpen, StreamOpenResult), PositionedStream with StreamEvent::Item / Gap / Resumed / BackfillDone / Disconnected, live and backfill runs and split(), StreamStats, AckMode::OnReceive / Explicit, cursors; every stream's queue is bounded (ClientConfig::stream_queue_bytes, plain streams report RawStreamEvent::Dropped); after disconnect().keep_streams() streams wait and Commander::resume_streams() resumes them; DynPositionedStream and the Python PositionedStream (docs/api/stream_reliability.md, docs/python.md). Tested end to end against a hand-written device: S4 host stuck, S6 host restart, resume after a reconnect (wire_weaver_client/src/event_loop/stream_e2e_tests.rs). Generated clients open streams through it (tests/streams_reliable, API-31); the dynamic client and Python pass the stream function's arguments and return its result. Missing: counted and reliable streams on trait paths (events carry the absolute path), the reconnect itself (EX-10), lossy-medium scenarios (TEST-19).

items.title: Transports and protocols (TR)
items.text:
• ✅ TR-1 ww_framer: packs many small messages into one packet or splits a big one across packets; U2Head with 1 byte overhead, CRC, recovery from missed frames, fuzzed.
  • ✅ TR-2 ww_link: link setup, device info, API version exchange.
  • ✅ TR-3 USB, RTT, WebSocket, UDP and in-process (messages, or simulated USB: real USB framing and packet sizes, in_process::usb_device).
  • ✅ TR-4 USB CDC-NCM: WebSocket over a USB network adapter, with a DHCP server so the host gets an address by itself, ping and a hello page over HTTP (examples_mcu/rp2, ww_ws_ncm); UDP the same way (ww_udp_ncm).
  • ✅ TR-14 Link tap · v0.5 — what crosses a link, recorded at the transport edge (docs/transport/tap.md): ww_tap (no_std Tap / NoTap; records are streams of the LinkTap trait: session, link events, frames and messages each way, client map), taken by every wire_weaver_client transport and event loop (ClientConfig::tap, tap::default_recorder(); TraceEvent / RegisterTracer an adapter over it, the iceoryx2 USB tracer removed) and by ww_device's FramedTx / FramedRx (with_tap; with NoTap a G0 firmware is the same size). ww_framer::pieces(frame) shares FramedRx's head code, no callbacks in the framer. Recorder batches into pooled 64 KiB ww_tape blocks (STD-42) flushed when full or after flush_time (10 ms), no allocation in steady state, losses counted in LinkEvent::Lost. wire_weaver_client::tap::Decoder: frame ↔ message linkage, cross-check against the message records, framer and link statistics, request/reply pairing by seq feeding the TOOL-9 explain code. E2E tests over simulated USB (tap/e2e_tests.rs, wire_weaver_cli cmd/tap/tests.rs): shared packets, split replies, a lost packet, stats, captures replayed identically. Open: the tap of a ww server's clients (ClientMap records are defined, nothing writes them yet).
  • 💡 TR-5 USB CDC-NCM extras — test on Windows, macOS, iOS and Android; serve files from an SD card over HTTP; mass storage with a README.
  • 📋 TR-6 CAN · v0.5.x — server and client, using CANopen (docs/transport/overview.md).
  • 📋 TR-7 UART · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 TR-8 IP / WireGuard · v0.5.x.
  • 💡 TR-9 EtherCAT.
  • ✅ TR-13 RTT server panicked on the first request — since TR-12 the async Server::handle checked for a waiting request with embassy_futures::poll_once(rx.wait_message()), a no-op waker; the RTT medium waits on an embassy_time::Timer while no data is there, and embassy-time panics on a waker not from its executor ("Found waker not created by the Embassy executor"). Every RTT device reset on its first request, the host saw no LinkSetup (examples_mcu/nucleo_g0b1re ww_rtt and an embedded_bedrock template firmware on Donguru, 16 Oct 2026). Fixed: the check polls once with the calling task's waker (ww_device server.rs poll_once_here); checked on Donguru over RTT through a J-Link. USB was not affected (no timer in its read).
  • 💡 TR-10 One-shot connect — no link setup at all: the host sends the API hash and its requests in one go; when the hash matches, the device runs them right away, else it answers with its hash and drops them and the normal setup follows. With message aggregation both arrive in one packet or frame, so a request over LoRa or LTE-M costs no extra round trip (introspection skipped by hash, CLT-7). Open: replayed and duplicate packets (CLT-17), which requests may run unannounced, how the hash is versioned. Needed by ww_dfu updates over slow links.
  • 💡 TR-11 MQTT / store-and-forward transport — devices offline most of the time pick up a retained message on wake (an update plan, config), replies queued on the broker. Look at MQTT-SN and LwM2M first.
  • 🚧 TR-12 USB throughput on small MCUs — measured with ww usb-loopback on Donguru (STM32G0B1, Cortex-M0+ 64 MHz, USB FS behind the board's HS hub, 15 Oct 2026). Done: U2Head encodes and decodes whole bytes in u32 instead of bit by bit (ww_framer framed.rs, was ~15% of the device's CPU per packet); the async device server flushes replies at once when no other request waits instead of after the accumulation window (ww_device Server::handle; DFU transcripts +1-2 packets). WireWeaverClass::with_endpoints() lets firmware allocate the endpoints, e.g. double-buffered bulk ones (Donguru, embassy-rs/embassy#7275: raw bulk 500 -> 950 kB/s OUT on the G0); usb_init_with_endpoints() offers the same choice to callers of the single-function usb_init() convenience, who can't reach into its private UsbBuffers. Next: CRC through a pluggable checksum so MCUs can use their CRC unit (~13% of the CPU per packet on the M0+); a host-side flush for lone requests that keeps packetization deterministic (flushing whenever the event loop goes idle made the DFU transcripts vary between runs); the same reply flush for the blocking server.

items.title: Introspection (ww_self, INT)
items.text:
• ✅ INT-1 API model AST with syn-style Visit/VisitMut, sent by devices as introspection data.
  • ✅ INT-2 Bundles recording crate versions, signatures of skipped traits and types.
  • ✅ INT-3 Relocated #[flag] fields in introspection data and dynamic serialization.
  • ✅ INT-4 Bit-aligned integers in ww_self: U1..U64, I2..I64 and nibbles are in the model (UB / IB, Nibble) and the dynamic client and Python read and write them, also as struct fields and enum payloads (done with SW-48); checked byte for byte by the conformance matrix (TEST-23, bits.*, struct.bits, enum.sub_byte.*).
  • 📋 INT-5 Documentation pass on ww_self · v0.5 — doc comments are missing (TODO in ww_self/src/lib.rs).
  • 📋 INT-6 sized / final_structure on ww_self types · v0.5 — where a type is unlikely to evolve, to make introspection data smaller. Can't be undone later, so decide per type.
  • 📋 INT-9 TailBytes and TailSize in the API model — a user type with a TailBytes (SW-9) or TailSize<N> (SW-18) field can't be in an API: the crate walker doesn't find the types (Type TailSize not found, Module shrink_wrap not found for shrink_wrap::tail_bytes::TailBytes), and ww_self::Type has no form for them, so the dynamic client and Python can't read or write them. Conformance cases tail_bytes, struct.tail_size.
  • 📋 INT-10 #[default] values in the API model — the crate walker records only that a field has a default (Field::default is a placeholder Bool(false), a TODO in wire_weaver_core's get_default_attr), so the dynamic client and Python read a field missing from older data as its type's default: #[default = 7] timeout: u16 reads as 0. Convert the default expression (literals, None, Some(..), unit variants) to a value and use it in the dynamic decoder; mind that Field::default is part of API signatures. Conformance case evolution.new_reads_old.
  • 📋 INT-11 Instance and Param have no conformance case — found by the coverage guard (TEST-25): ww_self::generics::prepare (API-43) turns every Type::Instance into an OutOfLine reference to a monomorphized struct/enum before any client sees a bundle (a device's own bundle is prepared too), and Type::Param only remains inside the now-unreferenced generic definition, so neither is reachable from any property's resolved type. Testing them needs a conformance mode over the introspection bundle's own wire encoding, not over app-level property values as the corpus does now.
  • 💡 INT-7 Compress ww_self strings with a pre-shared dictionary — partly addressed by leaving snapshot-known traits and types out of introspection data.
  • 💡 INT-8 Model enums that tolerate newer variants — the ww_self enums (Type, ApiItemKind, Fields, ...) and ww_numeric::NumericAnyType are no_future_version (SW-47): a host reading a newer model fails as a whole. With Unknown handled in every walker (visitor, signature, inline, values, compat, CLI, Python), an older host could show the rest of a newer device's API and mark the unknown parts.

items.title: Evolution, versioning and compatibility (EVO)
items.text:
• ✅ EVO-1 Evolution rules in docs/evolution/rules.md: crate layers and version bumping.
  • ✅ EVO-2 SHA signatures of APIs and types, hashing only the major version (or 0.minor), version independent.
  • ✅ EVO-3 Crate version recorded in bundles.
  • ✅ EVO-4 Global traits referenced by hash, global type registry (ww_global).
  • ✅ EVO-5 API snapshots of ww_global and ww_stdlib (wire_weaver_snapshots, ww api save), left out of introspection data and put back by the client.
  • ✅ EVO-6 Evolution checker and report: ww api check / ww api diff (docs/evolution/checker_tool.md).
  • ✅ EVO-9 Skipped definitions from another revision · v0.5.x — codegen keeps every definition it leaves out of a device's introspection data in ~/.wire_weaver/definitions/ by signature; a host that doesn't find a skipped definition under its signature in its snapshots (a device built from another revision of an unpublished crate) takes it from there and compares it by the evolution rules, with a warning instead of an error. Not found anywhere: an error with both signatures and the fix. Rust client, ww and Python (docs/std_library/ww_self.md, wire_weaver_client compat::tests::other_revision). #[cfg] enum variants don't change signatures (tests/cfg_variants).
  • 💡 EVO-7 Git dirty flag — not implemented, although the old tracker had it as done: neither ww_version nor codegen record git state. Uncommitted API changes are still caught, since they change the API's SHA signature. Firmware git info (sha, dirty, branch, tag) can be exposed through ww_firmware_info's bedrock_build_info stream. Decide whether the link or version also needs it.
  • 📋 EVO-8 Snapshots of crates.io crates — depends on "Load API crates from crates.io" above.

items.title: Tooling: CLI, GUI, Python (TOOL)
items.text:
• ✅ TOOL-1 ww CLI: list with filters, introspect as a resource tree (--raw-as-sent, --types), dynamic shell completions (docs/cli.md).
  • ✅ TOOL-2 ww api save / check / diff for API bundles and snapshots.
  • ✅ TOOL-3 ww api scaffold generates server handler stubs and the matching ww_codegen! call.
  • ✅ TOOL-4 Python module talking to any device, API built from introspection, dynamic values serdes, RTT built in (wire_weaver_py, docs/python.md).
  • ✅ TOOL-5 Runtime literals: values to bytes at runtime (eval, dynamic values).
  • ✅ TOOL-10 ww usb-loopback link test · v0.5 — round trips with lost and corrupted counts, host → device and device → host speed, on the sans-IO event loop (wire_weaver_client/src/event_loop/core/loopback.rs, windowed so a slow device holds the host back; e2e test against ww_device::Server in device_e2e_tests.rs), with a summary table and tuning options. Works with any device, the link layer answers. Checked on a full-speed board (Donguru, 3 hubs): about 155 round trips/s, 375 kB/s host → device, 317 kB/s device → host with 1 KiB messages.
  • ✅ TOOL-11 Dynamic observe — decodes a level's PropertyUpdate from introspection alone (CLT-28): DynResource::observe() / observe_blocking() (observable_properties() lists what it can ask for), reusing the CLT-28 event-loop routing and subscription sharing through a schema-less DynUpdate/DynConfig pair; ww observe <path> [--rate MS] prints each update's values, rate and link bytes/s (wire_weaver_client::DynObserver, wire_weaver_cli/src/cmd/observe.rs, tests/observe); wire_weaver_py's Node.observe(cfg) iterates the same updates as dicts. ww_self carries the sparse flag a dynamic decoder needs (DER-13).
  • ✅ TOOL-12 ww settings dump · v0.5 — host decoder of a ww_settings::Store flash dump, no device needed: ww_settings::dump::analyze (pages, every item slot valid/cut/garbage/erased, the current record of every key cross-checked against a real Store over the same bytes through fake_flash::FakeFlash) and decode_group for a caller that knows the concrete SettingsGroup type; ww settings dump FILE --word-size --page-size [--base] [--format text|json] in wire_weaver_cli (docs/cli_reference.md#ww-settings).
  • ✅ TOOL-14 ww monitor, ww stats, ww capture, ww explain FILE · v0.5 — the link tap (TR-14) in the CLI (docs/cli_reference.md#ww-monitor): live decoded print at the frame, link or API layer (--bytes, --bits for the TOOL-9 bit map of every message), framer and link statistics every few seconds or of a capture, captures with the device's API bundle in them, read back by ww explain FILE exactly as monitored live. Blocks come from a Feed (wire_weaver_cli/src/cmd/tap.rs): the CLI's own connection today, a ww server's tap of all its clients later. Global --monitor[=frame|link|api] (--monitor-bytes, --monitor-bits) and --capture FILE on every command that connects print (to stderr) or save that command's own connection, with the same Monitor, LiveFeed and TapeWriter; the tap decoder orders a block's records by time so a reply is paired with its request (docs/cli_reference.md#ww-monitor).
  • 🚧 TOOL-6 Dev GUI / web tool · v0.5.x — wire_weaver_tool (egui, Trunk) shows the AST and generated code. Goals: a web tool like the pest playground, a dynamic UI for any API (MVP prototyped), widgets per type, mockup server UI. See docs/dev_tool.md.
  • 💡 TOOL-7 Generated Python wheel for a specific API — nothing is generated for Python yet: examples/blinky_py is a hand-written pyo3 wrapper around the Rust client, and wire_weaver_py is dynamic. Generating typed pyo3 bindings from an API crate might be useful (see the TODO in docs/api/folder_structure.md).
  • 📋 TOOL-13 Some(None) in Python values — Python (and the conformance corpus, which uses its form) writes None for both None and Some(None) of an Option<Option<T>>, so the inner None can't be written or told apart when read. Needs a marker for a present None (e.g. ww.Some(None)). Conformance case option.option.some_none.
  • 📋 TOOL-8 ww inspect / read / write all GPIOs on any device · v0.5.x.
  • 🚧 TOOL-9 Buffer visualizer / "explain" encoding · v0.5.x — each bit traced to the value it belongs to. Done: ww_self::explain (the dynamic decoder records every value, length, discriminant, flag and padding with its front bits and back nibbles); ww_self::expr (feature expr: values and calls written as Rust expressions, Config { mode: Mode::Fast, .. }, motor.set_speed(1.5, Dir::Cw), motor.limit = 3, read by the type with errors naming the field) and wire_weaver_client::expr (the same with ww_si quantities, q!(3300 mV)); wire_weaver_client::envelope (a whole request or event: the ww_client_server envelope field by field, the payload by its resource); ww explain WHAT HEX | --value EXPR | 'call(..)' [--request], ww explain request|event HEX. Captures and the live link: ww explain FILE / ww monitor --layer api --bits (TOOL-14), replies explained by their request's seq. Open: payloads under a global trait path, multi requests and property updates; Series columns and sparse-struct slot headers in detail; shell completion of types and paths; a ww call on the same expressions; a GUI view (hex pane + tree, like Kaitai's Web IDE); Python explain() and expression input.
  • ✅ STD-1 ww_client_server — the request/event model, pruned of sideband/subscribe/rate, variable length seq numbers.
  • ✅ STD-2 ww_version.
  • ✅ STD-3 ww_si and ww_numeric.
  • ✅ STD-4 ww_date_time.
  • ✅ STD-5 ww_gpio.
  • ✅ STD-16 Common errors — ww_error::CommonError (Unsupported, InvalidArgument, InUse, Busy, WrongState, NoPower, Refused, Timeout, Fault, bounded strings), re-exported as wire_weaver::prelude::CommonError, nested first in an error enum as #[common] Common(CommonError) (the derive adds From<CommonError> and HasCommon); recognised by tools by its type (ww_self::TypeOwned::is_common_error): Python RemoteError.common with the doc line as the message, ww api tree -t marks it. Display by hand until DER-12 takes over. Every ww_stdlib API crate with fallible methods uses it except ww_dfu (its Error has no lifetime and predates this; only Unsupported/Busy would map cleanly, left as a follow-up) and ww_can_bus (not ready yet); ww_client_server's ErrorKind is a framework/link-level error, not an API error, so it is out of scope. docs/std_library/ww_error.md, tests/common_error.
  • ✅ STD-19 ww_pwm — Pwm / PwmChannel outputs (set_output, set_duty, stop, state), PwmCapture / PwmCaptureChannel measurements (frequency, duty, pulse width, edge count) over a plain stream with sideband Open / Close. Full rustdoc, mock server and in-process tests (tests/io_pwm), docs page (docs/std_library/ww_pwm.md) (STD-13).
  • ✅ STD-17 ww_timebase — Clock: device time as ww_si::Second (full width via now(), truncated elsewhere), sync master / slave (IRIG-B, PPS), sync_status, a time_map stream mapping device time to shared time, set_time_of_day for a master. tests/io_timebase, docs/std_library/ww_timebase.md.
  • ✅ STD-18 ww_adc — Adc, AdcStream (sideband Open / Close), AdcCapture. Fill-in done: full rustdoc, tests/io_adc mock server (one test per trait), docs/std_library/ww_adc.md, API snapshot (STD-13).
  • ✅ STD-20 ww_onewire — OneWire: addressed transactions with strong pull-up, reset, paged and bit-level (triplet) ROM search, the real Dallas/Maxim search algorithm. Full rustdoc, docs page (docs/std_library/ww_onewire.md), API snapshot, in-process test with a mock bus (tests/io_onewire).
  • ✅ STD-23 ww_si / ww_numeric extended · v0.5 — quantity groups and host helpers as cargo features, Second as a device timestamp (wrap rule, host Unwrapper), constructors, conversions and comparisons across prefixes and storage, UVlq32 / UVlq64 storage, Baud for baud rates (STD-13), Ratio, Torque and Timed<T> (EX-11). docs/std_library/ww_si.md, docs/std_library/ww_numeric.md. Zero-overhead typed quantities (Volt<u16, Milli>) are not part of it.
  • ✅ STD-38 ww_si 0.2: one generic Quantity<U: Unit> · v0.5 — every quantity is Quantity<U> { prefix, value, PhantomData<U> } with a zero-size marker per unit in ww_si::units and the 0.1 names as aliases (KiloGram → Gram); Dim, Scale, UnitExpr, Unit (own markers in API crates), Per / Times; constructors, quantize, conversions (to_si_f64 through each unit's scale), with_prefix, same_repr, comparisons, Display / Debug / defmt written once; unit algebra checked by the compiler against a product table verified at compile time; units::by_name. Same bytes on the wire as 0.1. docs/std_library/ww_si.md, ww_stdlib/ww_si/tests; the 0.2.0 snapshot holds Quantity, every marker and Per / Times, so devices leave them out of their introspection data. Other crates' call sites moved to the new constructors; the motor demo's own helpers (units.rs) and Load units are the follow-up piece; BaseUnit is replaced by STD-37 (run-time units).
  • ✅ STD-37 ww_si units known only at run time · v0.5 — SIExpr<'i> { Named { name, symbol, dim, scale }, Mul, Div, Pow } (recursive through RefBox, API-44) and AnyQuantity<'i> { prefix, value, unit }: the marker model on the wire, Dim as seven 4-bit exponents (sized), Scale too. A marker's UnitExpr maps one to one onto an SIExpr (Unit::SI_EXPR, SIExpr::of, SIExprOwned::from; back == and known()), shown, named and converted to SI by the same code as typed units, walks bounded by MAX_UNIT_DEPTH. ww_adc::ChannelInfo::unit is one; BaseUnit, SIExp, INib8P3 are removed. docs/std_library/ww_si.md#units-known-only-at-run-time (byte layouts), ww_stdlib/ww_si/tests/dynamic.rs, tests/io_adc. Dynamic clients, ww and Python show an AnyQuantity like the typed quantity of its unit (CLT-31's DynQuantity, both rendered by the public ww_si::tree walk), a device's own unit with its dimension and scale; writes take any quantity whose unit has a dimension. tests/quantities (an AnyQuantity property through the in-process transport), wire_weaver_py/tests.
  • ✅ STD-43 ww_si without wide integers on small targets · v0.5 — comparisons, with_prefix, the exact arithmetic and the integer conversions of quantities work on ww_numeric::Integer (sign and a magnitude as wide as the widest enabled number type): with types up to 32 bits only u32 code, no i64 / i128 and no f64 without float types. to_i32_in / to_u32_in / to_u32_wrapping_in; to_i128_in only with 64- or 128-bit types. 6 KiB less flash on Donguru (thumbv6m, opt-level = "z"). docs/std_library/ww_si.md#conversions-and-comparisons, ww_stdlib/ww_si/tests/narrow.rs and ww_stdlib/ww_numeric/tests/integer.rs (run with 32-bit types only too).
  • ✅ STD-24 ww_firmware_info / ww_board_info / ww_uid / ww_user_info device contract · v0.5 — the info crates every device implements. FirmwareInfo const items FIRMWARE (name, version, git, build time, profile), BUILD_ID (GNU build id, finds the ELF) and optional BUILD_RECORD; build::emit() + firmware_summary!() for build.rs, build_id() reader; LastReset (ResetRecord with a Fault per architecture behind cortex-m / riscv, stack words, boot_count, clear). BoardInfo::BOARD with RevisionSource. Uid::IDS, first id is the primary one (USB serial). UserInfo with bounded name / optional notes, UserInfoError, CAPABILITIES and the persistence rule. Docs docs/std_library/ww_{firmware_info,board_info,uid,user_info}.md, tests tests/{firmware_info,board_info,uid,user_info}. The const items are served by get_ handlers until constant items come from the introspection data; properties cannot carry #[errors] yet.
  • 🧪 STD-26 ww_log defmt over reliable streams · v0.5 — ww_log_bare_metal renamed ww_log. LogDefmt { const DEFMT (encoding, build id); frames() }: a reliable stream whose unit is one defmt frame, whole frames per item (up to 512 B), so lost is the exact number of dropped messages and logs from before the host connects arrive by resuming the device's session. LogText { records(); rw level: LevelFilter } with bounded LogRecord, Severity without User, LogError on CommonError. Device side: new crate ww_defmt_logger (global_logger!, lock-free ring with whole-frame commits, RTT tee that never blocks (whole frames or skipped and counted, whatever mode a probe set), pump() into the store, drops reported in place), ring stress-tested on the host with concurrent producers. tests/log_defmt decodes with defmt-decoder end to end; examples/defmt_log (host) and examples_mcu/rp2's rp2_usb_log (USB and RTT at once, build id in flash). docs/std_library/ww_log.md. Tested 16 Oct 2026 on Donguru B153A (STM32G0B1, typec_dongle API-10, with a PersistentRamRing): logs over USB and RTT at once, lost exact under a flood of 1000 (227 + 773), logs from before connecting and from before a forced HardFault; the non-blocking RTT tee with probe-rs attached (it sets the channel to blocking): floods of 1000 go on at ~62 us a line instead of ~620 us, RTT shows what fits. Known gap: frames dropped at the end of a burst are reported (lost) only with the next frame the device logs, so a quiet device shows the loss late. rp2_usb_log not run (no Pico 2 probe on the mesh). ww log in the CLI is a later item.
  • ✅ STD-25 ww_counters on cnt words · v0.5 — the device's cnt counters as raw buffer words, decoded on the host with the firmware's ELF found by its build id: Counters::INFO (format, used/capacity words of RAM and backup, build id), read(buffer, offset) pages of UVlq32, reset, optional watch stream (not served by anything yet); read_words / reset_words serve cnt buffers, feature host has WwSource (a cnt_core::Source). ww counters read|watch|tui|reset|info shows the cnt_view views (CLT-10). In the cnt repo: cnt::ram_used_words(), word sources and ELF lookup by build id in cnt_core, cnt_view, and the probe path checks the build id too. Docs docs/std_library/ww_counters.md, tests tests/counters; cnt_core / cnt_view 0.5 from crates.io.
  • ✅ STD-27 reset-record-age · v0.5 — ww_firmware_info::ResetRecord::boots_since_crash: boots since the crash data was saved (0 = the last reset was the crash), so a record kept across later normal resets shows how old it is. bedrock_crash counts it (Crash::boots_since) and the firmware template fills it.
  • ✅ STD-28 ww_indication lightweight rework — cut to one required item: mode: Mode (AllOff / OnlyEssential / Normal). brightness: Brightness (5 levels, one setting for all indicators), identify(duration) (blink everything to find the unit on a bench, errors on CommonError) and NAMES (indicator names, API-36) are each their own #[optional] item. Dropped alert_brightness / AlertBrightness, animation_enable, test_mode / TestMode and HAS_NOT_CONTROLLABLE. Docs docs/std_library/ww_indication.md, tests tests/indication (mock servers with only mode, and with every optional item).
  • ✅ STD-29 ww_can_bus on the stdlib idioms — from simple bridges to bus debuggers. Can is one controller: six required items (capabilities(), configure(CanConfig) answering what was set, config(), the observable status, the counted rx stream, the tx credit sink) and #[optional] set_mode (incl.
